title: Doubt belongs
hook: doubt belongs to every tradition's saints: Thomas doubted out loud and was still in the room eight days later
tomorrow: on a holy day, a boy whistled in the middle of prayers. then what?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: just breathing, the way Job's friends sat in silence. This week's lines come back in the games: on paper, study, keep one thing, smaller, not stopped, lying down counts. Now a different kind of break.
screen: `JUST BREATHING.` → `THIS WEEK'S LINES.` → `A DIFFERENT KIND OF BREAK.`

segments.voice: Someone says something huge happened while you were out, and you say: pics, or it didn't happen. Thomas said nearly that. The other disciples told him they'd seen Jesus risen. Thomas, called Didymus, the twin, had missed it. His answer: "Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe."
screen: `PICS, OR IT DIDN'T HAPPEN.` → `THOMAS MISSED IT.` → `I WILL NOT BELIEVE.`

segments.voice: Here's the surprise. John says that after eight days the disciples were inside again, "and Thomas with them." He didn't leave. He doubted from inside the circle. And Jesus came and offered him exactly what he'd asked for: the hands, the side. Thomas answered, my Lord and my God. Churches remember him as Saint Thomas the Apostle, with the doubt still attached to his name. He isn't alone. In Mark, a father pleading for his son cries, "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief." And at the very end of Matthew, on the mountain, "they worshipped him: but some doubted." Then Jesus sends them all out, the doubters too. That's the teaching inside these scenes: in the Gospels, doubt is met, not thrown out. For a rule of your own, a doubt doesn't cancel the practice. You can bring it into the room.
screen: `AFTER EIGHT DAYS, THOMAS WITH THEM.` · `HELP THOU MINE UNBELIEF.` · `BUT SOME DOUBTED.` · `DOUBT IS MET, NOT THROWN OUT.` · then, large: `DOUBT BELONGS.`

segments.voice: Say one honest doubt out loud, quietly, in plain words. Don't answer it or argue with it. Then stay where you are for the rest of the sit, the way Thomas stayed in the room.
Doubt belongs: doubt can live inside a practice, as it did for Thomas, who doubted and stayed.
Your line: doubt belongs. Thomas asked to see the hands, and was shown. That's the week, day 1673.
